question: Can you describe God?
answer:
God is the Giver of life [cdad6eaa77d2a85e], and God loves you [e8775eb6bb80b58a]. God is spoken of as the Father, who is greater [9b18f46fa9b7eb3e], and as the Creator, who has perfect faith in His creations because He created them [919b31be6a7b9305]. His work is wholly lovable and wholly loving, and this is also what you are [736705be8d1dfa40]. Indeed, the Kingdom of Heaven is you — for what else but you did the Creator create [2e867dcfd97baed2]?

Alongside this, love is everything [4168538feef0d380], and only the Oneness of knowledge is conflictless [3420d0187622a6e6]. Truth is always abundant [abd1b87ef5302ce0], and a pure mind knows the truth, which is its strength [24ec88551506aa54].

These passages describe God through His giving, His love, His fatherhood, and His creating, and they tie His nature to oneness, love, and truth. They speak to God in relationship — as Giver, Father, Creator, and as the very Kingdom you are — rather than offering a single definition of His nature apart from that relationship.

question: What does the Course say a miracle worker does?
answer:
The sole responsibility of the miracle worker is to accept the Atonement for himself [bcdee8e700d2ceef]. This means recognizing that mind is the only creative level, and that its errors are healed by the Atonement; once he accepts this, his mind can only heal, and he is placed where he can undo the level confusion of others, giving them the message that their minds are similarly constructive and their miscreations cannot hurt them [bcdee8e700d2ceef]. The miracle worker is one who accepts a true kind of denial and projection, uniting his own ability to deny and project with that true use, and imposing them back on himself and others, which establishes the total lack of threat anywhere [95eaa50303ea9c1b].

The power to work miracles belongs to you; you need to be ready and willing, since you are already able, and doing them brings conviction through accomplishment [1910b050bd79821d]. The ability is the potential, the achievement is its expression, and the Atonement is the Purpose [1910b050bd79821d].

Miracles themselves are all the same, with no order of difficulty among them [fc7c936bdc462f92], and they are healing because they supply a lack, performed by those who temporarily have more for those who temporarily have less [df2164815e50a849]. Miracles restore the mind to its fullness, and it is the duty of the released to release their brothers [85e9a97cd188972c]. All healing is the release from fear, so to undertake it you cannot be fearful yourself [a3c6653d355acf00].

Taken together, these show the miracle worker's work as acceptance first and extension second: accepting the Atonement for himself, and from that healed mind releasing others from their own belief in threat [bcdee8e700d2ceef] [85e9a97cd188972c] — that connecting of the pieces is my reading of how they fit, not a single statement made as a whole.

question: What is the Atonement?
answer:
The Atonement is the Purpose [1910b050bd79821d], and it is THE remedy [b385e07ab930fc06]. It works through correction and release: when you feel guilty, know that it is the ego that has violated the laws of God, not you [61d2aae6cbfaecf8]. You are told to leave the sins of the ego aside -- that is what the Atonement is for [61d2aae6cbfaecf8]. But until you change your mind about those your ego has hurt, the Atonement cannot release you, for as long as you feel guilty the ego is in command, since only the ego can experience guilt [61d2aae6cbfaecf8]. Accepting the Atonement is itself a process -- a series of pragmatic steps toward accepting it as the remedy [b385e07ab930fc06].

Its correction is bound up with forgiveness and healing: forgiveness is an empty gesture unless it entails correction, otherwise it is judgmental rather than healing [bb8dd5cfa83202da]. Those who are forgiven are freed, and they forgive in return -- it is the duty of the released to release their brothers [85e9a97cd188972c].

These passages show the Atonement by what it is for and how it releases you, rather than giving a single full definition of its nature; what's here centers on its purpose, its remedy of guilt, and its link to forgiveness and release.

question: What is the ego?
answer:
The ego is a man-made attempt to perceive yourself as you wished to be, rather than as you are [9f178f8b19409ac1]. It is nothing more than a part of your belief about yourself [565777c2ba4e3219]. It belongs to the realm of consciousness and perception rather than to knowledge or creation [9f178f8b19409ac1], and it depends on the specific — it is tied to the part of the mind that believes your existence means you are separate [4ed350b2b65dad8f].

The ego is bound up with guilt: only the ego can experience guilt, and as long as you feel guilty the ego is in command [61d2aae6cbfaecf8]. This need not be [61d2aae6cbfaecf8].

The self you made is something man reacts to with love and protection, much as God reacts to His Souls — but the real question is not how you respond to the ego, but what you believe you are [99889442ed8d213c].

Taken together, these describe the ego as a self-made image rooted in the belief in separation and sustained by guilt — not as your true identity. question: What is the mind?
answer:
The mind is one -- there is only one mind [0ec7063db717ac05]. By nature it is abstract [4ed350b2b65dad8f], and it carries real creative power: if it elects to, it becomes a medium by which the Soul creates along the line of its own Creation, and if it does not freely elect this, it still retains that creative potential [68d854b5e507e7c9].

The mind can split. When it does, only part of it splits, and so only part of it becomes concrete -- and that concrete part is the same part that believes in the ego and believes your existence means you are separate [4ed350b2b65dad8f]. The ego itself is a device for maintaining the belief that you are a separate thing, and it endures only through your willingness to use it [3deb7e322787da14][4ed350b2b65dad8f].

The mind can also be changed. To change your mind means to place it at the disposal of true Authority [68d854b5e507e7c9] -- to change it to think with God's [2dcd201fa0a1b4e2]. When the Son of God commends his spirit into the hands of his Father, the mind awakens from its sleep and remembers its Creator; all sense of separation disappears [d813e5f31f71e596].

Taken together, these describe the mind as one, abstract, creative, and free to choose -- either placing itself under the ego's device of separation or awakening to its Creator. They give us the mind's power and its choice rather than a single formal definition; what's offered here is its nature shown through what it does and what it can elect.
